title: Vegan diet in hereditary tumour syndromes
summary:
Lynch syndrome is a hereditary disease that greatly increases the risk of bowel cancer and other types of cancer. People with this predisposition have a very high risk of developing at least one of these cancers in the course of their lives, especially bowel cancer at a young age. These cancers are caused by genetic defects that impair DNA repair.
Apart from the use of specialised endoscopic procedures and preventive surgery, there are no treatments available to prevent the development of cancer in these patients.
Inflammation in the body also plays a role in the development of cancer, including colorectal cancer. Certain diseases that cause inflammation in the bowel, such as ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, can increase the risk of bowel cancer. Certain bacteria in the gut can also promote inflammation and cancer.
There is evidence that aspirin, an anti-inflammatory drug, can reduce the risk of developing bowel cancer in people with Lynch syndrome. This suggests that reducing inflammation may play an important role in the prevention of cancer.
Diet also has a major impact on inflammation in the body. Studies have shown that a diet that is low in fat and high in vegetables, such as a vegan or vegetarian diet, can reduce inflammation and lower the risk of certain types of cancer.
The planned study will now investigate whether a vegan diet rich in plant-based foods and free of animal products can reduce inflammation and lower the risk of developing colorectal cancer and other cancers associated with Lynch syndrome in people with the condition. The study will focus on how such a dietary change affects the immune system and metabolism and whether it can help prevent cancer.

interventions.name: 2-week vegan diet (before planned routine surveillance endoscopy)
2-week ketogenic diet (before planned routine surveillance endoscopy)
Control (regular diet, no change in dietary behaviour before scheduled routine surveillance endoscopy)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Genetically confirmed Lynch syndrome
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Ability to swallow plant-based foods
- Body mass index (BMI) ≥ 20 kg/m2 - Haemoglobin > 9 g/dl
- Normal leucocytes
- Creatinine < 1.5 mg/dl or calculated creatinine clearance ≥50 mL/min - Uric acid < 6 mg/dl
- Fasting glucose > 65 mg/dl
- Total bilirubin < 2 mg/dl or < ULN
- Written informed consent
- Willingness and ability to perform blood, stool and urine tests
    Ability to remain in daily contact (by phone or email) with study personnel to communicate important clinical information, including daily body weight, blood pressure, health status and adverse events during the diet
Exclusion criteria:
- Unintentional weight loss ≥ 5% in the last 3-6 months
- Known HIV infection
- Existing or planned pregnancy (positive pregnancy test in women, e.g. ß-HCG test in urine/serum) or breastfeeding
- Diagnosis of type I or type II diabetes mellitus requiring medical treatment
- Fasting glucose > 200 mg/dl
- Impaired renal function (creatinine > 1.5mg/dl; GFR <50%)
- Impaired liver function (total bilirubin > 2 mg/dl or AST/ALT 2-fold ULN
- Post complete colectomy
